feature_contract.scope_boundary: Only the R84 DX9Ex +TIME stage direct versus queued D3DXSprite Draw/Flush/End ownership and batch-lifetime transitions; exclude timer logic, GOAL content, original input/FFB, SkyGlow and world rendering, menu/HUD repositioning, DX11, frozen DXVK and R26 rollback.

subcomponents: Guard all direct +TIME and GOAL separation, early queue transitions, scope restore and foreign Draw drain against exact direct GPU batch ownership.
Guard queued stage boundary replay with matching live SpriteNode identity and epoch and negative regressions for stale epochs, recycled nodes, mixed buffers, failed flush and invalid metadata.

diagnosis.original_evidence: Original-game read-only resource/decompilation mapping in docs/automation/OUTRUN_VR_REA_RESOURCE_EVIDENCE_20261018.md identifies stage producer 0x00498670 and distinct sprite/numeric branches; Quest3 runtime outcome has not been demonstrated.
source_trace: Stage animation and numeric original call families reach scoped producer identification and the exact sprite source in src/hooks_uiscaling.cpp.
HudCommandBatch tracks active D3DXSprite Draw provenance, queued flag, queueNode and queueEpoch across source-scope boundaries and deferred Flush/End.
The R84 render path's source admission can become incorrect if an old queued D3DX GPU batch is treated as a later direct or differently queued owner during deferred physical GPU execution.
diagnosis.root_cause: The previous deferred D3DX source exit and stage/GOAL queue boundary guards checked producer, scope and flushability without additionally requiring the physical batch's queue-node/epoch ownership to match the current submission mode. Source-scope lifetime alone could not prove GPU-batch ownership.
alternatives_rejected: Do not globally flush queued D3DXSprite calls at every source exit or convert all world/GOAL draws to stage ScreenHud; unproven mixed batches must preserve original fallback.
Do not infer binocular HMD correctness from static source instrumentation or Windows CI; Quest3 physical evidence is still required.
